what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 4: A rest energy from binding: do composite bodies of two walkers fall like everything else?. SETTING (blocks 53 and 54; open PRs titled 'ail53: no master clock' and 'ail54: a phase timed by the local clock'; both are SUPPLIED clauses, not adopted; the axioms memo docs/MINIMAL_AXIOMS_2026-06-29.md defines no time metric and no amplitude dynamics). BLOCK 53: every site of Z^3 has a positive tick rate w_x, u = log w; the rate at a site is determined by its six neighbours' rates by one rule, covariant under translations and proper rotations, and scale covariant (only ratios of rates mean anything). ESTABLISHED there: every such rule has the weak-field form u_x = average of u over the six neighbours (no mass term); on a torus only the zero-sum part of a source enters; a record enters as a ratio kappa of its rate to its neighbours' mean, that is as the additive source log kappa (exact superposition; clocks slow near records if kappa < 1); ONE NUMBER, kappa, is left, and the second order of the rule is not fixed ((p - 1) d^2/6 for the power mean of order p). BLOCK 54: one moving record is a two-component amplitude psi_x (the site's qubit as its content; rotations turn the content as a direction); hermitian, rotation-covariant nearest-neighbour generators have the symbol a_0 + 2a sum cos k_j + beta sum sigma_j sin k_j; the walk with the qubit as coin is H = sum_j sigma_j D_j, D_j = (i/2)(T_j - T_j^dagger), energies +-sqrt(sum sin^2 k_j), velocity operator sigma_j (T_j + T_j^dagger)/2, and NO 2x2 matrix anticommutes with it (one walker has no rest energy). CLAUSE: the amplitude at a site advances in that site's own time, giving the generator w H, similar to the hermitian H_w = sqrt(w) H sqrt(w), conserved sum |psi_x|^2/w_x. ESTABLISHED: in a uniform gradient H_w^n T_a = lambda_a^n T_a H_w^n exactly (force = -(energy) x grad u in every state); rays of E = w(x) eps(k) obey dv_j/dt = -w^2 sum_l d_j d_l(eps^2/2) d_l u + 2 (v.grad u) v_j, which for the walk is -w^2 cos(2 k_j) d_j u + 2 (v.grad u) v_j whatever the rest energy; EXECUTED, NOT PROVED: packets follow clouds of rays to 5 parts in 10^4 (line) and 2 parts in 10^3 (three dimensions), and they also drift SIDEWAYS along (gradient) x (motion) by g T/(2k) (measured -0.119 and -0.227 against 0.120 and 0.240), which no ray has. Controls: .claude/science/physics-loops/admissibility-induced-law-20260906/specs/supervisor_control_block54_*.py on the block 54 PR branch. TASK: one walker has no rest energy (nothing in M_2(C) anticommutes with the three content matrices). (a) Take two walkers on Z (the reduced walk with sigma_z D, and then on Z^3) with a contact attraction V delta_{x,y} (and, separately, a nearest-neighbour attraction); find the two-body bound states of total wave vector K and their energy function eps_bound(K); show whether eps_bound^2 = M^2 + c^2 K^2 + O(K^4) and with what limiting speed c (is it the single walker's?). (b) Put both walkers in the same rate field under block 54's clause, the INTERACTION INCLUDED in what the local clock times (the whole generator is multiplied by w, symmetrized); show that a small bound state has the energy function w(X) eps_bound(K) and so falls at -grad u at rest, whatever V. What happens if the interaction is NOT timed by the local clock? (c) State what this does to the statement 'rest energy needs a larger site algebra' (parked entry 4 of docs/repo/DEFERRED_DECISIONS.md is not to be touched or re-raised; the question is only whether binding supplies a rest energy inside M_2(C)). check.py: exact diagonalization on a ring for the bound-state dispersion, and a propagation of a bound pair in a gradient.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/composite-bodies-rest-energy-without-a-larger-site-algebra/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py.
